name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: The set was empty. B's short, uncritical reviews helped put its mean (7.75) above A's (7.0). This reason names review quality; R05 names a specific missed issue and R08 a rating that contradicts its own text.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: The set was empty. The committees did not see different facts; they weighted the same facts differently. R05 covers an issue that only one committee saw.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: The set was empty. A alone questioned the core motivation and the closest competitor, and A's area chair kept both as required revisions. R06 covers issues that both committees saw.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: The set was empty. B's area chair, not B's reviewers, carried the oral. This reason names who decided; R02 names what a decision rested on, and a reviewer can also make that kind of claim.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The set was empty. The response moved f6JJ's score and B's area chair called it 'particularly good', but no A score moved. R07 covers score changes that come from other reviewers, not from the response.

name: Recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact
justification: The set was empty. B's oral rests on a forecast of impact beyond BNNs, and the paper does not test that forecast. R01 covers an area chair who decides alone; this reason covers the content of the argument, from any member of a committee.

name: Reviewer discussion moved one committee's scores
justification: The set was empty. oG66 credited the other reviewers, not the authors, for the raise. R03 covers score changes that the response causes.

name: Reviewer's rating out of line with own text
justification: The set was empty. FCVA's 6 sits below its own positive text and lowered the mean that A's area chair leaned on. R04 does not fit: FCVA spent 10 hours, so the problem is the rating, not inattention.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's scores rest on less scrutiny. Reviewer_yA7o spent 2 hours, did not check the proofs, and its update names no gap; Reviewer_6Pv4 did not check the claims. A's reported hours average 4.0, B's 6.3.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw dense notation and no experiments. A's area chair made 'very difficult to follow' the verdict, and Reviewer_yA7o held the missing experiments against the paper. B treated readability as fixable, and Reviewer_kvzq wrote 'I don't think that can be held against the work'.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A's Reviewer_h23K said that Theorem 2's surrogate set turns the problem back into MGT. The paper confirms it, the response did not answer it, and it underlies h23K's 6. B's Reviewer_kvzq called the criteria 'a strict generalization'.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: B's area chair chose an oral that no reviewer asked for. B's top score was 8 ('Top 50% of accepted NeurIPS papers'), and the meta-review gives only 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution' as grounds.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved B's Reviewer_iUkv from 5 to 6 ('they have clarified my main concerns'), and B's area chair cited that raise. No A score moved; Reviewer_yA7o read the response and kept its concerns.

name: Unsure reviewers defaulted to a borderline score
justification: Three of A's four reviewers said they could not judge the paper and rated 6, and A's area chair took the flat 6s as the verdict. In B only Reviewer_iUkv said so; B's other reviewers rated 8 and 7. R04 does not cover this: Reviewer_rBKj spent 7 hours and read closely, so its 6 shows doubt, not inattention. R08 does not fit, because these reviews state no verdict for the 6 to contradict.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's only score above 7, Reviewer_1UMR's 8 at confidence 2, rests on a two-sentence main review that names no weakness and did not check the math. A's reviews also carry less scrutiny than B's other three: A averaged 3.0 hours against B's 4.0, and two A reviewers misstated the main bound as linear in k.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the first coreset for decision trees, weak exposition and thin related work. B's area chair judged the novelty 'absolutely above the bar' and treated the writing as fixable in revision. A's area chair gave the same praised novelty a poster.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B raised the gap between single-tree theory and the forest and boosting experiments, the uncited database-histogram work and the Algorithm 2 flaw. Reviewer_nDd9's 4 rests partly on the first two, and B's meta-review lists 'comparison to past work' among its 'very substantial concerns'. These concerns helped put B's mean below A's, though B's area chair still chose an oral.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
justification: B's area chair chose an oral that no reviewer asked for. B's ratings (4, 7, 7, 8; mean 6.5) sit below A's poster ratings (mean 6.67). B's meta-review calls the writing 'almost of the level of being considered unpublishable', and its 'absolutely above the bar' appears in no public review or comment.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's top score came from a thin review. Reviewer_xycR's 9, the only 9 among the seven reviews, rests on a 2-hour, one-paragraph review with 'one minor comment'. Reviewer_LgSM's 8 rests on general praise and a raise that names no specific point. The careful reviews are close (A: 7, 7; B: 7, 8). A's one thin review, Reviewer_FCFz's, gave 8.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw that the work builds on prior ideas: A's Reviewer_yauQ named C-learning, and B's Reviewer_6QWr called the rationale 'not necessarily novel'. A's area chair read the paper as 'a mix of existing and new tools'. In B, Reviewer_6QWr still called the work 'very high quality', and B's area chair named no weakness.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only A raised the simple image tasks and the claims with no linked experiment. Both points are correct, and the paper concedes the image limitation in Sec. 6. These doubts held A's Reviewer_3uQ8 at 7 after the rebuttal, while B's reviewers praised the experiments as 'comprehensive' and 'extensive'.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: B's only score above 7, Reviewer_rfa1's 9 at confidence 4, rests on three generic sentences ('clear, rigorous, and well written') and a list of presentation nits. It says nothing about the proofs, Algorithm 1 or the novelty over Zhang et al. (2020). Two more B reviewers rated 7 at confidence 1 without assessing the theory: Reviewer_nWYc knows 'very little about the technical details of causal learning', and Reviewer_4Bw1 gives no support for 'original and high quality'. Stage 1 finds no inattentive review in A.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees saw the same complete criterion, dense notation and idealized experiments. A's area chair called clarity 'the main shortcoming of the paper'. B's area chair quoted Reviewer_rfa1's 'clear, rigorous, and well written' and named no weakness, though Reviewer_1SfX, Reviewer_4Bw1 and Reviewer_3m9X called the paper dense, hard to parse or abstract.

name: Area chair followed one outlying reviewer
justification: B's area chair gave an oral with no reason beyond two quotes, chiefly Reviewer_rfa1's 'clear, rigorous, and well written', and named none of the weaknesses that Reviewer_1SfX, Reviewer_4Bw1 and Reviewer_3m9X raised. Without rfa1's 9, B's mean equals A's 7.0. R01 does not fit: it needs the chair's own reading, and B's chair gave none; it passed on one reviewer's verdict. R04 covers how thin rfa1's review is, not the chair's choice to let one reviewer outweigh four. R06 covers how the two committees weighted clarity, not how one chair combined its own reviewers.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
justification: A's scores rest on less scrutiny. A's top score, Reviewer_DcW4's 9, came after 2 hours with generic praise, no weakness or question, and the wrong claim that prospective coding 'has no precedence in the literature'. Reviewer_ob4X's 8 came after 2 hours in one paragraph. No A reviewer raised the prior work on fast population responses. B's 9 (Reviewer_iVNT) also admits confusion, but B's Reviewer_VGyX ran the code and checked the literature.

name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
justification: Both committees questioned whether the model's fast transmission between rate units is biologically realistic. A's Reviewer_BSPV called it 'this major caveat to the biological plausibility of the model', then raised to 7 on a promised limitations section, and A's area chair did not mention it. B's area chair made 'the timescales of synaptic transmission' a required revision. This cause is secondary: the specific points B weighed came from VGyX alone (R05).

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
justification: Only B's Reviewer_VGyX showed that faster-than-τm responses were known and uncited (Knight 1972; van Vreeswijk and Sompolinsky 1998). He also showed that the noise filter uses synaptic time constants of 0.1 to 2 ms. The camera-ready concedes both points. His 3 rests on them, and B's area chair made both required revisions, suggested a new title and stopped at a poster. No A reviewer raised either point.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
justification: The response moved A's Reviewer_BSPV up to 7 ('Based on the authors' response, I have revised my score to an accept') on the promise of a limitations section. No B score moved: Reviewer_VGyX stayed 'still convinced' at 3, and Reviewer_gRxq and Reviewer_iVNT kept 8 and 9.
